elements.name: AbnormalTraffic
elements.definition: A traffic condition which is not normal.

members.name: abnormalTrafficType
members.definition: A characterization of the nature of abnormal traffic flow, i.e. specifically relating to the nature of the traffic movement, implying a level of service.

members.name: numberOfVehiclesWaiting
members.definition: The number of vehicles waiting in a queue.

members.name: queueLength
members.definition: The length of a queue or the average length of queues in separate lanes due to a situation.

members.name: relativeTrafficFlow
members.definition: Assessment of the traffic flow conditions relative to normally expected conditions at this date/time.

members.name: trafficFlowCharacteristics
members.definition: The consistency (steadiness) of the traffic flow.

members.name: trafficTrendType
members.definition: A characterization of the trend in the traffic conditions at the specified location and direction.

elements.name: AbnormalTrafficTypeEnum
elements.definition: Descriptive terms for abnormal traffic conditions specifically relating to the nature of the traffic movement, implying levels of service.

members.name: stationaryTraffic
members.definition: Traffic is stationary, or very near stationary, at the specified location (i.e. average speed is less than 10% of its free-flow level).

members.name: queuingTraffic
members.definition: Traffic is queuing at the specified location, although there is still some traffic movement (i.e. average speed is between 10% and 25% of its free-flow level).

members.name: slowTraffic
members.definition: Traffic is slow moving at the specified location, but not yet forming queues (i.e. average speed is between 25% and 75% of its free-flow level).

members.name: heavyTraffic
members.definition: Traffic is heavy at the specified location (i.e. average speed is between 75% and 90% of its free-flow level).

members.name: unspecifiedAbnormalTraffic
members.definition: There are abnormal traffic conditions of an unspecified nature at the specified location.

members.name: other
members.definition: Other than as defined in this enumeration.

members.name: poorRoadSurfaceCondition

members.name: undisclosed

members.name: unknown

members.name: accident
members.definition: Accidents are situations in which one or more vehicles lose control and do not recover. They include collisions between vehicle(s) or other road user(s), between vehicle(s) and fixed obstacle(s), or they result from a vehicle running off the road.

members.name: accidentInvolvingHazardousMaterials

members.name: accidentInvolvingHeavyLorries

members.name: accidentInvolvingMassTransitVehicle

members.name: multipleVehicleAccident

members.name: alertCLocationName

members.definition: Unique code within the ALERT-C location table which identifies the specific point, linear or area location.

elements.name: AlertCLocationCode
elements.definition: A positive integer number (between 1 and 63 487) which uniquely identifies a pre-defined Alert C location defined within an Alert-C table.

elements.name: AlertCMethod2Linear
elements.definition: A linear section along a road between two points, primary and secondary, which are pre-defined in an ALERT-C location table. Direction is FROM the secondary point TO the primary point, i.e. the primary point is downstream of the secondary point.

elements.name: AlertCMethod2Point
elements.definition: A single point on the road network defined by reference to a point in a pre-defined ALERT-C location table and which has an associated direction of traffic flow.

elements.name: AlertCMethod2PrimaryPointLocation
elements.definition: The point (called Primary point) which is either a single point or at the downstream end of a linear road section. The point is specified by a reference to a point in a pre-defined ALERT-C location table.

elements.name: AlertCMethod2SecondaryPointLocation
elements.definition: The point (called Secondary point) which is at the upstream end of a linear road section. The point is specified by a reference to a point in a pre-defined ALERT-C location table.

elements.name: AlertCMethod4Linear
elements.definition: A linear section along a road between two points, primary and secondary, which are pre-defined ALERT-C locations plus offset distance. Direction is FROM the secondary point TO the primary point, i.e. the primary point is downstream of the secondary point.

elements.name: AlertCMethod4Point
elements.definition: A single point on the road network defined by reference to a point in a pre-defined ALERT-C location table plus an offset distance and which has an associated direction of traffic flow.

elements.name: AlertCMethod4PrimaryPointLocation
elements.definition: The point (called Primary point) which is either a single point or at the downstream end of a linear road section. The point is specified by a reference to a point in a pre-defined ALERT-C location table plus a non-negative offset distance.

elements.name: AlertCMethod4SecondaryPointLocation
elements.definition: The point (called Secondary point) which is at the upstream end of a linear road section. The point is specified by a reference to a point in a pre-defined Alert-C location table plus a non-negative offset distance.

elements.name: DataValue
elements.definition: A data value of something that can be measured or calculated. Any provided meta-data values specified in the attributes override any specified generic characteristics such as defined for a specific measurement in the MeasurementSiteTable.

members.name: dataError
members.definition: Indication of whether the value is deemed to be erroneous by the supplier (true = erroneous). If not present, the data value is assumed to be ok. This may be used when automatic fault detection information relating to sensors is available.

members.name: reasonForDataError
members.definition: The reason why the value is deemed to be erroneous by the supplier.

members.name: accuracy
members.definition: The extent to which the value is expected to be free from error, measured as a percentage of the data value. 100% means fully accurate.

members.name: computationalMethod
members.definition: Method of computation which has been used to compute this data value.

members.name: numberOfIncompleteInputs
members.definition: The number of inputs detected but not completed during the sampling or measurement period; e.g. vehicles detected entering but not exiting the detection zone.

members.name: numberOfInputValuesUsed
members.definition: The number of input values used in the sampling or measurement period to determine the data value.

members.name: smoothingFactor
members.definition: Coefficient required when a moving average is computed to give specific weights to the former average and the new data. A typical formula is, F being the smoothing factor: New average = (old average) F + (new data) (1 - F).

members.name: standardDeviation
members.definition: The standard deviation of the sample of input values from which this value was derived, measured in the units of the data value.

members.name: supplierCalculatedDataQuality
members.definition: A measure of data quality assigned to the value by the supplier. 100% equates to ideal/perfect quality. The method of calculation is supplier specific and needs to be agreed between supplier and client.

elements.name: Date

elements.name: DateTime

elements.name: EuBodyworkCodeEnum
elements.definition: Bodywork codes according to REGULATION (EU) 2018/858.

members.name: aa
members.definition: Saloon - A vehicle defined in term 3.1.1.1 of international standard ISO 3833:1977, fitted with at least four side windows.

members.name: ab
members.definition: Hatchback - A saloon as defined in REGULATION (EU) 2018/858 Annex 1 Part C Ref. 2.1 with a hatch at the rear end of the vehicle.

members.name: ac
members.definition: Station wagon - A vehicle defined in term 3.1.1.4 of international standard ISO 3833:1977.

members.name: ad
members.definition: Coupé - A vehicle defined in term 3.1.1.5 of international standard ISO 3833:1977.

members.name: ae
members.definition: Convertible - A vehicle defined in terms No 3.1.1.6 of international standard ISO 3833:1977. However, a convertible may have no door.

members.name: af
members.definition: Multi-purpose - A vehicle other than AG and those mentioned in AA to AE in tended for carrying persons and their luggage or occasionally goods, in a single compartment.

members.name: ag
members.definition: Truck station wagon-Vehicle defined in term No 3.1.1.4.1 of ISO 3833:1977. The luggage compartment must be compl. sepated from the passenger compartment. And the ref. point of the driver's seating pos. must be min. 750mm above the surface supp. the veh.

members.name: ba
members.definition: Lorry - A vehicle that is designed and constructed exclusively or principally for conveying goods. It may also tow a trailer.

members.name: bb
members.definition: Van - A lorry with the compartment where the driver is located and cargo area within a single unit.

members.name: bc
members.definition: Tractor unit for semi-trailer - A towing vehicle that is designed and constructed exclusively or principally to tow semi-trailers.

members.name: bd
members.definition: Road tractor - A towing vehicle that is designed and constructed exclusively to tow trailers other than semi-trailers.

members.name: be
members.definition: Pick-up truck - A vehicle of a maximum mass not exceeding 3 500 kg in which the seating positions and the cargo area are not located in a single compartment.

members.name: bx
members.definition: Chassis-cab or chassis-cowl - An incomplete vehicle with just a cabin (complete or partial), chassis rails, power train, axles, which is intended to be completed with bodywork, customised to the needs of the transport operator.

members.name: ca
members.definition: Single-deck vehicle - A vehicle where the spaces provided for persons are arranged in a single level or in a way that they do not constitute two superimposed levels.

members.name: cb
members.definition: Double-deck vehicle - A vehicle defined in paragraph 2.1.6 of UN Regulation No 107.

members.name: cc
members.definition: Single-deck articulated vehicle - A vehicle defined in paragraph 2.1.3 of UN Regulation No 107 with a single deck.

members.name: cd
members.definition: Double-deck articulated vehicle - A vehicle defined in paragraph 2.1.3.1 of UN Regulation No 107.

members.name: ce
members.definition: Low-floor single-deck vehicle - A vehicle defined in paragraph 2.1.4 of UN Regulation No 107 with a single deck.

members.name: cf
members.definition: Low-floor double-deck vehicle - A vehicle defined in paragraph 2.1.4 of UN Regulation No 107 with a double deck.

members.name: cg
members.definition: Articulated low-floor single-deck vehicle - A vehicle that combines the technical features of codes CC and CE.

members.name: ch
members.definition: Articulated low-floor double-deck vehicle - A vehicle that combines the technical features of codes CD and CF.

members.name: ci
members.definition: Open top single deck vehicle - A vehicle with partial roof or without roof.

members.name: cj
members.definition: Open top double deck vehicle - A vehicle without roof over all or part of its upper deck.

members.name: cx
members.definition: Bus chassis - An incomplete vehicle with just chassis rails or tube assembly, power train, axles, that is intended to be completed with bodywork, customised to the needs of the transport operator.

members.name: da
members.definition: Semi-trailer-Trailer that is des. and constr. to be coupled to a tractor unit or converter dolly and to impose a subst. vertical load on the towing vehicle or converter dolly. The coupling for a vehicle comb. shall consist of a king pin and a fifth wheel.

members.name: db
members.definition: Drawbar trailer-Trailer having at least two axles, with at least one is a steered axle:(a)equipped with a towing device which can move vertically (in relation to trailer); (b)that transmits less than 100daN as static vertical load to the towing vehicle.

members.name: dc
members.definition: Centre-axle trailer- see definition in REGULATION (EU) 2018/858 Annex 1 Part C Ref. 5.3.

members.name: de
members.definition: Rigid drawbar trailer- see definition in REGULATION (EU) 2018/858 Annex 1 Part C Ref. 5.4.

members.definition: The refill point is not occupied, has got enough energy resources and can be used.

members.definition: The refill point is not accessible because of a physical barrier, e.g. a car.

members.definition: The refill point is currently in use for charging.

members.definition: The refill point has got a fault.

members.definition: The refill point is not yet active or it is no longer available (deleted).

members.definition: The refill point is in use, this might include vehicle charging activity.

members.definition: The refill point is currently out of order.

members.name: removed
members.definition: The refill point was discontinued/removed.

members.name: unavailable
members.definition: There is no energy available at this refill point. This could be because of a failure or damage or a longer lasting delivery failure (note that there is a literal 'outOfStock' for a short-term shortage).

members.name: unknown
members.definition: The status of the refill point is unknown (can also be offline).
